summary: Brunei waives visas in tiers — 90 days for US, Canadian and European passports, 30 days for several Asian, Gulf and European nationalities, and 14 days for most ASEAN neighbors — while Australians and four Gulf nationalities obtain a visa on arrival and most other travelers apply in advance for a visit visa through a Bruneian mission.

declarations.name: Brunei E-Arrival Card
declarations.text: Foreign visitors must submit the E-Arrival Card online before travelling to Brunei — it may be requested at check-in. Register on the Immigration Department's portal imm.gov.bn, then create the card under 'Travel Cards'. You do not need one if you are not passing through immigration.

source.name: UK FCDO — Brunei travel advice, entry requirements

currencyLimits.text: No official source we could read states Brunei's cash-declaration threshold; the customs department's website publishes none. The UK's travel advice says to declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty, through the Customs.BN app or on arrival at the airport.

source.name: Immigration and National Registration Department, Brunei Darussalam

notes: Alcohol is not sold anywhere in Brunei. Non-Muslim visitors aged 17+ may import a limited duty-free allowance (commonly two bottles of spirits or wine plus twelve cans of beer), must declare it on arrival, and must observe the minimum interval between imports.
Brunei applies sharia-influenced law: drug trafficking carries the death penalty, and importing publications deemed offensive to Islam is prohibited.
Cigarettes have no duty-free allowance. Declare them and pay duty on arrival.

payments.text: Cards are accepted in hotels, malls and larger restaurants in Bandar Seri Begawan, but small eateries, water taxis and markets are cash-based. Singapore dollars are accepted at par alongside the Brunei dollar.

safety.text: Brunei has very low crime and is among the safest countries in Southeast Asia. The main considerations are legal and cultural: strict rules on alcohol, drugs and public behavior apply to visitors as well as residents.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Brunei travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: January to April tends to be somewhat drier; expect hot, humid equatorial weather with short downpours in any month.

idp.text: Brunei is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Brunei is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Brunei yet.

tips.text: No alcohol is sold in Brunei. No bars, no restaurant service. Non-Muslim visitors may bring in a small duty-free allowance for private consumption and must declare it at customs on arrival.
Brunei imposes the death penalty for drug trafficking and severe penalties for possession — never carry anything through the border for someone else.
During Ramadan, eating, drinking or smoking in public in daylight hours is an offense for everyone, including non-Muslims, and many restaurants close until sunset.
Dress modestly, especially at mosques — cover shoulders and knees, and women should carry a headscarf; robes are lent at the main mosques.
Singapore dollars are legal tender at 1:1 alongside the Brunei dollar — leftover SGD from a Singapore stopover spends normally here.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Brunei?
faq.answer: Many visitors do not. US, Canadian and EU passport holders get 90 days visa-free, the UK 90 days, several Asian, Gulf and European nationalities get 30 days, and most ASEAN neighbors get 14 days. Australians and four Gulf nationalities obtain a visa on arrival, and remaining nationalities apply in advance for a visit visa through a Bruneian mission — no official Brunei source describes an online e-Visa.

faq.question: Do Australians need a visa for Brunei?
faq.answer: Australians obtain a visa on arrival, single or multiple entry, for stays up to 30 days. Bring the fee in cash: BND 20 for single entry, BND 30 for multiple entry.

faq.question: Can I drink alcohol in Brunei?
faq.answer: Alcohol is not sold anywhere in the country. Non-Muslim visitors aged 17 and over may bring in a limited amount (commonly two bottles plus twelve cans of beer) for private consumption, and it must be declared at customs on arrival.

faq.question: What is the Brunei E-Arrival Card?
faq.answer: A free digital arrival declaration that all foreign visitors must submit online before traveling to Brunei. It replaced the paper disembarkation card — complete it on the Immigration Department's website shortly before your trip.

faq.question: How long can US citizens stay in Brunei?
faq.answer: US passport holders can enter visa-free for up to 90 days — the most generous tier of Brunei's waiver scheme, shared with Canadian, EU and UK passports.
